page: Amazon Web Services c8g.metal-24xl is a bare-metal, compute-optimized server powered by 96 dedicated AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 physical cores on the arm64 architecture. Operating at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz, this instance features 192.0 GB of DDR5 memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. It operates without hyperthreading, allocating one thread per physical core. No local storage or GPUs are included in this bare-metal configuration, and network connectivity is supported by a 40 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark results position this server in the top tier for multi-core processing and memory throughput. The multi-core stress-ng and Geekbench tests rank in the top 10%, supported by high memory bandwidth scores, including 481.1 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 201.25 GB/sec for write operations. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, software compilation with Clang, and Passmark database operations also achieve top-tier performance. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the average and strong categories, respectively.

The server exhibits a clear tradeoff between massive parallel execution and single-threaded tasks. While Redis SET operations reach a top-tier 196.18 million operations per second and static web serving throughput is highly efficient at 102.43 GB/sec, LLM text generation for small 135M models is relatively weak at 60.64 tokens/sec. Conversely, text generation for medium and large models performs in the top 25%. Given the high core density, DDR5 memory bandwidth, and lack of local storage, this instance is highly cost-efficient for compute-heavy, scale-out workloads such as high-performance computing, multi-threaded software compilation, database operations, and high-throughput web serving.
